x: Ray Hall and George Beecham were always well placed and provided the backing for team honours. John Keown walked well to complete our scoring four and was closely followed by D.

Ken Bailey walked magnificently in his first Brighton, George Beecham took third place after a steady race, and John Keown backed up well. Thanks must go to those who assisted our walkers, to mention just a few, Eric & Mavis Hall, Jack Goswell, Eric Beecham, and Don Bartliff.
We congratulate Eric and Mavis Hall on their recent addition to the family.

My publicity managers not only found an old photograph of yours truly but I was prevailed upon (in an inebriated state) to sign it and when last seen it was being placed on the wall by the side of one signed by a Donald Bradman but I am not sure what event he was in! Photo: Mavis Hall
Regretably, we must also record the death on 17th July 1998 of Rose, wife of the late Tom Morrell and mother of Mavis Hall. Rose had survived Tom by just three years and eight hours.
Globe-trotters Eric and Mavis Hall wrote to us recently on Old Sydney Parkroyal Hotel notepaper to tell us that they had just completed climbing to the very top of the Sydney Harbour Bridge.
